card.name: "In" before adverse-event incidence figures
card.fires_on: The word "in" (or an opening parenthesis) right after "occurred" or "was reported", just before a patient count or percentage. It appears in adverse-reaction sentences from trial results.

modes.label: occurred/reported in
modes.description: "in" after an event verb, leading into the number of patients affected.

modes.label: Parenthesis after percentage
modes.description: An opening parenthesis after a percentage, introducing the count.

card.plain: It marks the spot in a safety-data sentence where the share of patients with a side effect is about to be given.
